acv.quote: Around ninety-five thousand a year. Ninety-five K ACV, on a two-year term.

header.reason: Martin, the CFO, saw only a side-by-side rate page. Nothing showed what failed orders cost Fernbrook. Sam blames price, but we never showed the value in their numbers.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Aim messaging at retailers losing big orders at checkout.
findings.why: Lucy came inbound because one in twelve online orders failed at payment, worse on big baskets.
findings.quote: one in twelve online orders was failing at the payment step

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Put the cost of failed orders in front of the finance decider.
findings.why: Martin decided from a rate-only page. Sam never met him, and Lucy carried our case alone.
findings.quote: Martin said no. Lucy told me. I never met him.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Prepare buyers for their bank cutting its rate to keep them.
findings.why: Lucy said the bank offered only a better rate. After that her questions moved from declines to rate.
findings.quote: After the bank came back, every email was the rate.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Keep explaining why big orders get declined and how we fix it.
findings.why: Farah's explanation of big-ticket declines had Lucy nodding, but it never reached Martin.
findings.quote: Lucy was nodding the whole way.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Build a one-page business case a buyer can hand to finance.
findings.why: Lucy asked for one for Martin. Sam sent the deck, and Farah's decline analysis never ran.
findings.quote: something she could hand Martin. Like a one-page business case.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Say 'orders dying at the last step' instead of 'declines'.
findings.why: Lucy described losing big baskets, like a four-thousand-dollar greenhouse, when the card says no.
findings.quote: orders dying at the last step
